video_title: Lamelo & Finch speak | The Jon Krawczynski Show

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: LaMelo Ball's underwhelming performance in his first press conference
quotes.excerpt: I do think that it was underwhelming in terms of LaMelo's just answers to questions, participation.
quotes.quote: I think that what I gathered from seeing the feedback from fans who watched it, who can't get enough LaMelo content right now, they are so interested and intrigued and excited about what this is going to look like. If I saw an overall reaction, I do think that it was underwhelming in terms of LaMelo's just answers to questions, participation that way, and I would just say that that part in particular was not a surprise to me. When you talk to people who have been around LaMelo, who know him well, who have covered him, who have worked with him, he is not a press conference guy. We are used to seeing the stars here like Anthony Edwards, like Karl-Anthony Towns, a lot of guys be these megawatt personalities in the media, but LaMelo is clearly not a press conference guy.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: LaMelo Ball's surprisingly nice and engaging personality behind the scenes
quotes.excerpt: He's incredibly nice. It sounds weird, but he's just a nice guy. He shakes hands, he is engaging.
quotes.quote: What did strike me, and I chatted with him for a few minutes afterward, talking to people around him, he's incredibly nice. It sounds weird, but he's just a nice guy. He shakes hands, he is engaging and he listens and he's not sort of like maybe this kind of flaky personality that from afar you look at the guy and you see him, he's driving these crazy cars and he has these all these tattoos everywhere and he plays this style of game that is sort of volatile. But the personality of him, Jim, is very soft-spoken, very engaging that way. And so I do think when you cast this thing forward, it's probably a good thing because I think Anthony Edwards is the gravity that holds the Wolves universe together.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: The Timberwolves' risky strategy in the Rudy Gobert and Mike Conley trades
quotes.quote: Tim Connelly is being characterized, rightfully so, as a big risk-taking general manager. He made the Rudy Gobert trade, made the Mike Conley trade, now he makes the D'Angelo Russell trade was a risk. The LaMelo Ball trade is being characterized as a risk, and I think rightfully so, given LaMelo's injury history, given that he hasn't played on a winning team, or on a playoff team since he's been in the league. And so you look at the Wolves side of this equation and say, yeah, that's a risk to send out Naz Reid and every remaining draft capital piece of draft capital that you have to bring in this player and to try to make it work.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: The Hornets' strategic patience in trading LaMelo Ball
quotes.excerpt: The Hornets clearly think that their biggest window for contention is going to come when Brandon Miller and Kai Jones are 24, 25, 26.
quotes.quote: One thing that hasn't really been talked about as much, I don't think, has been the risk-taking side of the Charlotte part of the equation because LaMelo was an incredibly popular figure in Charlotte with the Hornets franchise. He was the face of the franchise for the first five years of his time in Charlotte. And then you look at now they have Brandon Miller and they have Kai Jones and they have kind of an exciting young team that won a lot of games last year. And a lot of teams in that position would then go all in and say, okay, we finally had a winning season after so many years kind of in the gutter, let's go get Rudy Gobert, let's go add to this, get a veteran to bring in to this young team and really try and vault into contention in the Eastern Conference. And it's clear by the decision that Jeff Peterson and the front office made by sending them all, LaMelo here, is that they looked at last year's success and determined, you know what, we are not quite there yet. We are not going to try to expedite this process. We are not hiring Tibs to coach Levine and Wiggins and Towns. We are going to actually more so add another draft some more draft pick compensation, we are going to get LaMelo, a player that we really, really like, and we're sort of going to take a deep breath and wait a little bit more.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: Chris Finch's flexible approach to the Timberwolves' power forward rotation
quotes.excerpt: Finch is pretty adamant that he does not see Jaden McDaniels as a power forward.
quotes.quote: I talked to Chris Finch in Vegas about this, and I know that Chris Hines did as well, and what struck me and what was surprising to me was that Finch is pretty adamant that he does not see Jaden McDaniels as a power forward. That he still thinks that he keeps him at the three, he keeps him guarding the perimeter, and wants him kind of in more of like a wing playmaking, you know, shot creation mode on offense than he would be if he was playing power forward. And so, you know, Finch told me that he's actually envisioning being very malleable night-to-night on who gets those minutes depending on the matchup. One night it could be Terrence Shannon Jr. if they need a little bit more scoring punch in that role. One night it could be Jaylen Clark if they need kind of a stouter, defensive-minded player in that mode. One night it could be Trey Lyles if they're playing a bigger team and they need a little bit more height and a little bit more rebounding.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: The Timberwolves' goal to build a versatile, defensive-minded roster
quotes.excerpt: They're trying to show Anthony Edwards that they are an organization that he can rely on.
quotes.quote: I think that the Timberwolves, in all of these moves that they're making, and how aggressive they always are, they're trying to show Anthony Edwards that they are an organization that he can rely on to continually be aggressive to try to put him in the best positions to succeed and win that championship that he wants. If he thinks that he can do that elsewhere, he may go elsewhere eventually. But I think as long as the Wolves show that, hey, we've got you, we're going to take care of you, we're going to be good stewards of your career and you can depend on us to build a roster around you that at least is in the conversation for that, I think he very well could say, you know what, I will help you out a little bit. He makes a ton of money in endorsements, he has all sorts of other ventures going on. And so, you know, he will eventually have a decision to make in like a year or two if he wants to do that. But I do think that if this team continues to ascend and continues to play well, he may look at that and say, you know what, I'm going to follow in the footsteps of Jalen Brunson, Victor Wembanyama, others who will have to do it and and try and just give Tim Connelly and Alex Rodriguez and Mark Loriel all the opportunities to continue to kind of keep great players around me that I can.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: The Timberwolves' impressive WNBA roster depth and performance
quotes.excerpt: Olivia Miles has been an absolute revelation. Kayla McBride is playing as well as she has ever played.
quotes.quote: They haven't gotten anything out of Fisa Colley, or they've only had a little bit of contribution from Dorka Juhasz, so I think she's a very good player. Olivia Miles has been an absolute revelation. Kayla McBride is playing as well as she has ever played. She's an All-Star player and she's playing as well as she's ever played right now. Courtney Williams has been great both in leadership and it's just it's remarkable what they're doing in that franchise right now. And Cheryl Reeve keeps setting records. It just it's remarkable what they're doing in that franchise right now.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: Cheryl Reeve's coaching success and impact on the Lynx
quotes.excerpt: She is the best coach that's ever coached in the WNBA and she deserves all the recognition.
quotes.quote: First, congratulations to Cheryl Reeve for climbing the mountain in the win total in the WNBA. She is the best coach that's ever coached in the WNBA and she deserves all the recognition that she is getting and she you know, she has done an incredible job in with this group of quickly acclimating to what a dynamic player Olivia Miles is. And you know, it's it's only so often that we see a player come in and change everything about the feeling of a team to the degree that Olivia Miles has.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles is the most valuable player in the WNBA
quotes.excerpt: Olivia Miles right now is the most valuable because she has taken a team that has been shorthanded
quotes.quote: I know A'ja Wilson might be the best player in the league, she is the best player in the league, but Olivia Miles right now is the most valuable because she has taken a team that has been shorthanded, that is missing great players, and they are the number one team in the league and it is on Olivia Miles' back. It's been remarkable.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles has successfully reinvigorated teammate Natasha Howard
quotes.excerpt: She also seems to have reinvigorated Natasha Howard, as an older player who has just been
quotes.quote: She also seems to have reinvigorated Natasha Howard, as an older player who has just been, but Natasha keeps getting the ball right at the rim, she can finish. Great stuff. It's remarkable what they're doing in that franchise right now.

quotes.speaker: Jim Souhan
quotes.summary_phrase: Olivia Miles has transcended into mainstream casual sports conversation
quotes.excerpt: She's crossed over into the mainstream just casual sports conversation in a way that few others have
quotes.quote: Olivia Miles is such a ray of sunshine on this team and she is starting to transcend the conversation because I heard Bill Simmons on a podcast just last week just say, have you seen Olivia Miles to I think it was Chuck Klosterman and they were not talking about the WNBA a ton. He just said, have you seen this Olivia Miles yet? She's incredible. LaMelo Ball was asked about Olivia Miles at his press conference. She's crossed over into the mainstream just casual sports conversation in a way that Caitlin Clark, maybe Paige Bueckers, if only a few other WNBA players have, and it's her style of play, it's her personality, it's her effect on winning.
